family.tagline: A kitchen whiteboard, a garage workbench and a Companion Core, four lives.
family.story: Sally runs her small consulting practice from the craft room. John writes software at the garage workbench, Steve claims the den, and Jean studies in her shared bedroom. The apps they use run on one Companion Core in the kitchen.

members.name: Sally
members.work: consultant, runs her own small practice

companion.name: Juniper
companion.job: Drafts replies and proposals for Sally's clients, using the context she connected.
companion.limits: Juniper only drafts in this home. Sally reads and sends every message.

companion.name: Quill
companion.job: Opens supplier websites in its own browser and fills in the forms John asks for.
companion.limits: One form at a time. John reads each one and sends it himself.

popup.title: A parcel at the door
popup.body: A parcel waits at the front door, at the top of the stone steps. John carries it past the loggia to the kitchen, where Sally clears the sideboard.

popup.title: Unbox the Companion Core
popup.body: Inside: the Companion Core, a power cable, a quick-start guide and a recovery USB drive. Jean ticks each item off the guide as Steve unwraps it.

popup.title: Plug it in
popup.body: Sally plugs the cable into the Core and presses its button. It wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: Join it from a phone
popup.body: John joins the Core's own network from his phone's Wi-Fi settings, then picks the home network.

popup.title: Pick your first agents and apps
popup.body: In the Companion Hub store, Sally picks Hermes and John picks OpenClaw. Companion Memory (beta) comes along, with Joplin Server and Gitea. Then they walk away.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: Juniper says hello
popup.body: Sally messages the agent she named Juniper. A reply comes back, and the Core is running.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: sally
say.text: Hello, Sally. I am Juniper. What should we do first?

beats.capability: block ads, trackers and bad domains for every device on your network at the DNS level

popup.title: One ad blocker for home Wi-Fi
popup.body: After supper, four screens share the couch and the home Wi-Fi. John set up Pi-hole on the Core to block ad and tracker domains for devices that use it.

beats.capability: a family planner with a shared calendar, tasks, shopping, meals and notes

popup.title: The whiteboard has a twin
popup.body: Sally copies the whiteboard's week into Yuvomi, the family planner. Its calendar and shopping list sit on the Core, not in a calendar service.

beats.capability: a family planner with a shared calendar, tasks, shopping, meals and notes

popup.title: Saturday dinner, one shared list
popup.body: It is Steve's turn to cook on Saturday. He checks the week's meals in Yuvomi, then adds lemons to the shopping list on the Core that everyone shares.

beats.capability: read Wikipedia and other reference sites served from your Core

popup.title: A biology question, asked at home
popup.body: Jean checks how a cell divides in Kiwix, which serves Wikipedia from the Core. No search engine sees her question.
popup.note: The Wikipedia file is downloaded once.

beats.capability: the Obsidian note app in your browser; notes stay as local Markdown files

popup.title: A proof that finally makes sense
popup.body: Jean asks a model on the Core, in Open WebUI, why a proof works. The chat stays on the Core by default. She rewrites the answer in Obsidian.

beats.capability: translate text and documents on your own Core

popup.title: French homework, checked on the Core
popup.body: Jean writes a paragraph in French, then pastes it into LibreTranslate to see what it says in English. The words are translated on the Core, not on a translation website.

beats.capability: a searchable catalog of local-AI and self-hosting tools

popup.title: Jean goes looking for a project
popup.body: Jean wants a project for the school fair, so she searches Spellbook. It is a catalog of local-AI and self-hosting tools, and it runs on the Core.
popup.note: Crash reports go to Companion Intelligence unless switched off.

beats.capability: take notes and keep to-dos that sync across your devices through your own server

popup.title: Call notes sync to the Core
popup.body: The client call ends, and Sally types up the notes at her standing desk. They sync to Joplin Server, which sits on the Core, not with a note service.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: Juniper drafts, Sally sends
popup.body: A client wants a proposal by lunch. Juniper, her agent on the Core, drafts it from context in Companion Memory (beta). Sally reads it and sends it herself.
popup.note: Companion Agents and Companion Memory are in beta.

beats.capability: merge, split, compress and convert PDFs on your own Core

popup.title: One proposal, one file
popup.body: Before the proposal goes out, Sally merges it with the fee schedule in Stirling-PDF. The merge runs on the Core, not on a PDF website.

beats.capability: scan and file your paperwork; it reads every page, tags it and makes it searchable

popup.title: An invoice and a school form
popup.body: Sally scans a client invoice and a school form. Paperless-ngx reads and tags each page. The scans sit on the Core, not in a rented drive.

beats.capability: store every password in a vault you host that works with the Bitwarden apps

popup.title: A sign-in goes in the vault
popup.body: A client gives Sally a portal sign-in. She saves it in a VaultWarden vault, which works with the Bitwarden apps. It sits on the Core, not with a password service.

beats.capability: write code in VS Code in your browser, with the editor and your files on your Core

popup.title: An editor at the workbench
popup.body: John's laptop opens Code Server in a browser. The editor and his project files sit on the Core.
popup.note: Installing an extension reaches an outside registry.

beats.capability: host private Git repositories, pull requests and issues on your Core

popup.title: John pushes the last branch
popup.body: At the workbench, John pushes the day's last branch to Gitea. Its pull requests and issues sit on the family's Companion Core, not on a rented code host.

beats.capability: browser automation and tool use in a sandboxed app on your Core

popup.title: Quill fills in the form
popup.body: John needs brackets for the workbench. Quill opens the supplier's website and fills in the order form. John reads every field, then sends it himself.
popup.note: OpenClaw reaches websites over your home internet.

say.speaker: john
say.text: The form is ready. Check the delivery address before you send it.

beats.capability: run Steam on your Core and play it in a browser on a screen in the house

popup.title: Steve's game runs in the house
popup.body: After school, Steve signs in with his own Valve account. Steam Headless runs the session on the Core at home and shows it in a browser on the Den TV.
popup.note: Steam needs a Valve account. A Core may lack the graphics power a game wants.

beats.capability: stream your own movies, shows and music to every screen in the house

popup.title: Friday's film in the den
popup.body: Steve picks Friday's film. Jellyfin plays the family's own collection from the Core to the Den TV, not from a streaming service.

beats.capability: back up, search and organise your family photos and videos on your own Core

popup.title: School trip photos, backed up
popup.body: The school trip left Steve with a few hundred photos. They back up from his phone to Immich on the Core, not to a photo cloud.
popup.note: The first start takes a while.

beats.capability: track your plants, watering and care history across rooms and beds

popup.title: The lavender has a journal
popup.body: It is Steve's job to water the lavender by the stoop. He logs each watering in HortusFox, and the plant journal sits on the Core.

popup.title: One Core, four lives
popup.body: Paperwork, code, games and homework, all on one Companion Core beside the kitchen whiteboard.

closing.body: Your planner, paperwork, code and homework can run on a Companion Core at home. Browse the Companion Hub store and pick your first apps.

notes: garage-code uses Code Server, which has no QA screenshot: the owner must list garage-code (app-qa-screenshot) in reviewed.json. Not added here.
Open WebUI replaces ChatGPT and Claude, and the chip text 'replaces ChatGPT' trips cap-parity, so Open WebUI is only ever named in a beat's with, never as app.
den-session: Steam needs a Valve account (note), the Core may lack the GPU a game wants, no game titles, no frame rate; the session shows in a browser on the Den TV.
garage-errand: OpenClaw prepares the form, John reads every field and sends it. Carries the OpenClaw website note. No cloud key is mentioned anywhere.
Film (eight beats): plug-in, join, hello, kids-lookup, office-draft, garage-repos, den-session, outro. garage-code is kept out of the film because it needs owner review.
Sally, John, Steve and Jean are the flagship Brennan family; this home tells them in the Craft Room, Garage, Den and Kids Bedroom with the Core in Kitchen and Dining.
